subject: Latency targets, throughput fitment, and cost options — decision items
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: latency goals, streaming needs, and cost levers (recap)

Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and a few concrete asks so we can size a fit and put a proposal on your side.

Summary from our call:
- Primary product flow: user-facing chat assistant (multi-turn, enriched with catalog context).~100k monthly active users, peak 2.5k concurrent chat sessions.
- Performance goals: p95 end-to-end generation latency target = 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens), p95 = 700ms for medium prompts (<= 512 tokens). Streaming responses are preferred for UX; token-by-token acceptable as long as first-token latency <= 220ms.
- Throughput/concurrency: must support bursts up to 3k concurrent sessions for 10–30 minute windows during promotions. Sustained steady-state concurrency ~800.
- Cost sensitivity: total inference spend target <= $12k/month for hosted inference at launch (upper bound while we pilot).

Key technical tradeoffs we discussed and immediate levers to meet SLOs:
1) Continuous batching + autoscaling: batching reduces per-token overhead but increases first-token latency. We can use dynamic batch sizing with a small latency-aware floor to keep first-token within 220ms while improving cost.
2) Prefix/KV cache: for repeated contextual data (catalog), KV cache reduces compute for multi-turn flows; this is a high ROI for your workload.
3) Quantization & model variants: recommend starting with an 8-bit quantized Llama-2.1 variant for cost, with a 16-bit or fp16 fallback for worst-case latency-sensitive routes.
4) Streaming mode: enables first-token earlier via partial decode; combined with small initial batch it's the best UX/cost balance.

Asks / next steps for sizing:
- Can you share the per-session average prompt lengths and expected token distribution (short/medium/long)? (I attached a sample spreadsheet — fill the green column).
- Confirm whether catalog context is identical for all users in a session (yes/no) — this affects cache effectiveness.
- Any hard SLA or procurement constraints we should know before proposing reserved capacity? Procurement contact CC'd if you prefer a procurement-led path.

I'll run a quick cost simulation (continuous-batch vs. on-demand + KV cache + quantization profiles) and share two recommended configurations: "latency-first" and "cost-first."

Attachments: acme_latency_requirements.xlsx (please fill), reference cost model: redwood_cost_model_v2.pdf

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeretail.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency goals, streaming needs, and cost levers (recap)

Thanks Karthik — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Token distribution: roughly 60% short (<=128), 30% medium (129–512), 10% long (>512). I'll attach a CSV export from our analytics for the last 30 days by end of day.
- Catalog context: each session pulls a subset of the catalog (topical) that is stable within a session but varies between users — seems like a good fit for KV caching per session.
- Strict procurement constraint: we need a pilot rate card under $15k/month and a commitment window of 3 months max. We're flexible on a small reserved commit if the numbers make sense.

One more item: during promotions we anticipate a spike in concurrency to about 3k for up to 45 minutes, and we need graceful degradation (fall back to a cheaper model variant) rather than hard failures.

Jordan
Director, Product — Conversational CX
Acme Retail
jordan.price@acmeretail.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency goals, streaming needs, and cost levers (recap)

Appreciate the clarifications — attached is an initial sizing note and two config proposals. High level: 

Option A — Latency-first (meets p95 300/700ms targets reliably):
- Model: fp16 Llama-2.1-medium variant on dedicated instances (lower quantization risk).
- Runtime: small dynamic batching (max batch 32), streaming enabled, hold-time 20ms.
- Cache: session-scoped KV cache for catalog embeddings + prefix caching.
- Autoscale: warm pool + rapid burst capacity to handle 3k spikes; fallback policy to a quantized model variant if queueing >150ms.
- Estimated cost: $22k/month (hosted) — exceeds your pilot target but keeps latency headroom.

Option B — Cost-first (target under $15k pilot):
- Model: 8-bit quantized Llama-2.1-base variant for most routes, hybrid fallback to fp16 for critical flows.
- Runtime: continuous batching with aggressive accumulation on steady-state, but low-latency floor (hold-time 10ms) for first-token.
- Cache: aggressive KV cache and response caching for canonical prompts.
- Autoscale: more conservative reserved capacity, rely on model-variant fallback to degrade gracefully under spike.
- Estimated cost: $11–14k/month (hosted) depending on cache hit rate and burst hours.

Tradeoffs and what I need from you to finalize numbers:
1) Sample token-distribution CSV (Jordan said you'll share) — drives batch size recommendations.
2) A prioritized list of routes that must not degrade (e.g., checkout assist) so we can pin them to higher-tier config.
3) Confirmation whether you can accept a model-variant fallback for 3k-concurrency spike windows (we will route to quantized model automatically).

If you want, Marissa can put together an A/B plan and cost delta chart for Reservations vs. burst-on-demand. Rishi can run a quick micro-benchmark for the quantized variant and share p95 decode numbers.

I'll also include a short decision log in the next note so your procurement team has clear options.

— Karthik

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeretail.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency goals, streaming needs, and cost levers (recap)

Jordan — quick note to confirm next steps and owners so procurement has what they need: 
- Jordan: please drop the token-distribution CSV and flag the mission-critical routes (reply in this thread).
- Procurement: we'll produce a 3-month pilot rate card and a clear SLO appendix with fallbacks; expect the draft DocuSign link by Friday (linked above).
- Marissa (owner): I'll compile the A/B cost delta and a short decision log comparing Option A and Option B by EOD Friday.
- Rishi (owner): please run the quantized model micro-benchmarks (p50/p95 first-token and full-generation) and share numbers + brief methodology.

Attachments included with this thread: redwood_cost_model_v2.pdf (detailed assumptions).

Short-term acceptance criteria (what procurement will ask for): pilot <= $15k/month, SLO appendix describing graceful degradation behavior, and a rollback plan. We'll structure the pilot with a 2-week evaluation window after the first month to review metrics.

Thanks — Marissa
